author: Zack Priehs
title: Lansing police release 2025 end-of-year statistics - NewsBreak
text:
By Zack Priehs ,
1 hours ago LANSING, (Mich.) WLNS — Many mid-Michiganders have spent the last couple of weeks thinking about what’s in store for 2026 and looking back on 2025. The same can be said for the Lansing Police Department.
LPD says overall crime was down in 2025, including a 36% drop in shooting homicides and a 19% fall in non-fatal shootings. They credit much of this progress to their community partnerships.
Lansing Police Chief Robert Backus says he’s happy with last year but acknowledges that the police can’t do it alone and heavily rely on the community to be the boots on the ground.
“We know that our community groups have contact with people, they hear things, they have influences in places that we don’t as police officers,” Backus said “So if we’re gonna touch 100% of this community and address this problem the right way, we need to have a wide variety of partners.”
Backus tells 6 News he’s pleased with the progress local police made in 2025, a year in which they saw fewer shootings, a 17% decrease in burglaries, and a 13% drop in vehicle theft.
However, there was a 26% increase in robberies, something he says they’ve already taken steps to address. Additionally, he wants the public to know the best practices to stay safe.
“When people are alone, they become easier targets, so of course you can’t always avoid that. So, knowing that you’re safer when you’re in a group, or in a public space,” said Backus.
Overdoses were also down in 2025, although they were unable to provide exact numbers. Backus believes overdoses are down because there’s less drugs on the street and lifesaving drugs like Narcan are more accessible than ever. LPD recommends that people carry Narcan, and you can pick it up for free at LPD locations.
